column1: # Characteristic: how many components the model has and how they are arranged.
# NOTHING ELSE. Everything that proved to be an objective went to algorithms;
# everything that proved to be a function-class constraint went to attributes.
# See MODELS_AXES.md "Three things that look like topology and are not".

column5: one component maps input to output in one pass
column6: there is one body of parameters and one direction of flow
column7: there is a second component consuming the first's output, or a parallel tower
column8: most classifiers; GPT; BERT; NeRF; SVM; Gaussian process
column9: Renamed from `Single stack` on 2026-10-06 (owner). A stack means a stack of LAYERS, which asserts something false about an SVM or a Gaussian process even though the underlying claim -- this model has one component -- is true of them. The axis is NOT misapplied to non-neural models: random forest resolves to Ensemble, so topology separates forests from kernel machines correctly. Only the name was neural-centric. Its two children keep `stack` because they are genuinely layer stacks.

column5: every position may attend to every other
column6: the representation at a position depends on both sides of it
column7: positions may only depend on what precedes them
column9: This level was built inside the Transformer LINEAGE subtree by both derivation runs. It is topology: it applies to any family.

column5: a position may depend only on what precedes it
column6: the model can generate one step at a time from its own output
column7: positions see the whole input at once

column5: a second component consumes a representation built by the first
column6: two bodies of parameters, with a latent or memory between them
column7: one body of parameters, or two parallel towers over different inputs
column8: T5; BART; U-Net; autoencoders; VAE; MAE
column9: Autoencoders live here. An autoencoder IS an encoder and a decoder -- what makes it an autoencoder is the reconstruction TARGET, which is an objective and belongs to algorithms (owner, 2026-10-02).

column5: parallel components encode different inputs and are combined only at the end
column6: two or more bodies of parameters run side by side, joined by a comparison in a shared space
column7: one component feeds the next in sequence
column9: Collapsed with its sole child on 2026-10-02: a parent with one child is a rename of that child (R4). Re-split if a non-dual multi-tower family appears.

column5: many independent models are combined at prediction time
column6: members are trained separately and their outputs are pooled
column7: the components are jointly trained parts of one forward pass

column5: several separately trained components run in sequence, each consuming the previous one's output
column6: the stages are trained apart and composed at inference; a stage can be swapped without retraining the others
column7: the components are jointly trained parts of one forward pass, which is encoder-decoder, or run side by side, which is multi-tower
column9: Added 2026-10-06. Found twice over: a placement agent flagged multi-stage pipelines as homeless, and the topology audit independently reported stable_diffusion, dalle2 and segnet resolving by parents-column ORDER because their parents disagreed. Distinct from Encoder-decoder, where the two halves are trained together.
